newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk courts accept Kurdish language translators.
newsitem.headline: Turk courts accept Kurdish language translators.

text.p: Turkish courts have accepted the use of Kurdish language translators in cases where necessary, the Istanbul-based Kurdish Association for Kurdish Culture and Language Research (Kurtkav) said on Friday.
"We are happy and hopeful, as we see this as a change in the handling of the Kurdish problems. This is how it can be solved," Kurtkav chairman, Yilmaz Camlibel, told Reuters.
Kurtkav applied to the Justice Ministry two months ago to fill the gap for registered Kurdish translators in cases where witnesses do not speak Turkish.
"We are happy our application was granted. This shows that the Kurdish language has been recognised," Camlibel said.
Turkish authorities long denied the existence of a Kurdish language. Turkish court records previously read "he or she spoke in an unknown language..." when Kurdish was spoken in courts.
There are about 10 million Kurds in Turkey. Kurdish is not allowed to be taught at schools in Turkey and public use of Kurdish has been forbidden at different times in the country's history.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the 12 year-old conflict between Turkish troops and Kurdish rebels fighting for independence or autonomy in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
